messages:
Maya Singh: Quick ask for the launch bundle — need a field-ready battlecard that fits a 1-slide summary + 3 short rebuttals vs Cloud APIs and infra vendors. Keep language punchy for SDRs.

Evan Cruz: Got it. My approach: 3-line hero claims, 2 quick examples (failover + cost-savings), and a one-paragraph micro-bench. No heavy tables.

Priya Rao: Suggest hero claims: "Predictable tail latency (SLO-backed)", "Lower served unit cost via batching + prefix cache", "One API, any deployment: hosted, reserved, or private". Short, repeatable.

Maya Singh: Love those. Can we add one sentence to each that a salesperson can read in 10s? E.g., after the claim add "(keeps customer experiences stable during region incidents)".

Evan Cruz: Yep. I'll write the 10s speak: 
- Predictable tail latency — SLOs and fallback routes mean fewer customer-visible timeouts.
- Lower unit cost — smart batching & prefix caching reduce token spend without added engineering work.
- One API, any deployment — move from hosted to private without changing calls or rollouts.

Priya Rao: For rebuttals:
- Cloud APIs: "When upstream changes or limits occur we surface SLA-backed fallbacks and transparent routing so your app stays live."
- Infra vendors: "We deliver runtime kernel tuning and rollout automation so your infra team doesn't become the bottleneck."
- DIY self-host: "Skip the ops cliff: we handle quantization, batching, and KV cache ops in production."

Liam Chen: Micro-bench paragraph for PR (draft): "In a simulated cross-region failover test, Redwood Inference rerouted traffic to a compatible model variant and preserved 90-94% of baseline throughput with a median latency increase of ~180ms. Results vary by model and payload; tests run on 8k seq, median of 8 runs. The outcome: graceful degradation rather than application outage."

TechBot: Reminder: launch-battlecard-review scheduled tomorrow 11:00am PT. Invite posted to #marketing and #sales.

Maya Singh: Nice. Two conversion hooks for the webinar landing page A/B tests: 
A) "Same API. Better economics. Predictable latency."
B) "Keep features live during incidents — SLOs and smart routing."
Which one should the SDRs lead with in outbound?

Evan Cruz: For technical buyers use B. For product-led signups use A. Recommend tagging inbound leads by which line they responded to and routing accordingly.

Priya Rao: Routing play: tag demo requests with label "ops-risk" when they mention latency/uptime; SDRs escalate "ops-risk" to a solutions demo with Dedicated/offline private play. Otherwise route to standard hosted demo.

Liam Chen: I'll prep a single slide: left side 3 hero claims with 1-line salesperson speak, right side a tiny flowchart showing outage -> smart routing -> compatible variant -> shifted latency numbers + image alt text. No big tables.

Maya Singh: Perfect. Last asks before I lock the file: (1) final one-paragraph micro-bench copy for PR (2) one short line the field can use as the opener during demos. I'll pull a beta quote for the deck after review.

Evan Cruz: Micro-bench copy ready to paste: "Benchmark summary: In controlled failover tests Redwood Inference maintained ~92% throughput while adding ~+180ms median latency when routing to a compatible variant (tested on 8k sequences). This demonstrates controlled, graceful degradation and predictable recovery behavior for production apps."

Priya Rao: Field opener: "We give you SLO-backed latency guarantees plus cost levers like batching and prefix caching — so you can ship LLM features without surprise infra bills."

TechBot: Note: battlecard-review meeting in 60m. Attachments: slide draft + micro-bench PNG.

Maya Singh: Great work — I'll consolidate, tag design for the flow visual, and if the review is green I'll mark the battlecard field-ready and push to the webinar kit. Thanks team.
